newsitem.title: USA: CFTC gives nod to CBOT-LIFFE linkage, CBOT says.
newsitem.headline: CFTC gives nod to CBOT-LIFFE linkage, CBOT says.

text.p: U.S. regulators late Tuesday gave approval to the Chicago Board of Trade's linkage with the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) set to start Friday, a CBOT spokesman said.
Brooksley Born, chairwoman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, called CBOT President Tom Donovan to notify him personally of the decision, the spokesman said.
Donovan on Monday sent a letter to Born expressing frustration about the lack of CTFC action at this late stage in the process.
The CBOT is scheduled to begin open-outcry trading of LIFFE's German bund futures and options at 1020 CDT/1520 GMT Friday. LIFFE will also trade the CBOT's U.S. Treasury contracts.
In the letter Monday, Donovan called the delay in CFTC approval "another vivid illustration of the competitive disability the agency has imposed on U.S. exchanges."
CFTC officials were unavailable for comment late Tuesday.
